question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+y}{21}, & -3\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=0,$ find $\text{E}[3X+7Y].$
question.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[X].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[Y].$

The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}+y}{21}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{21}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+xy]}_{x=-3}^{x=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{21}[(\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}+3y)-(\frac{(-3)^{3}}{3}-3y)] \\  & =\frac{1}{21}[18+6y] \\  & =\frac{2(3+y)}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{2(3+y)}{7}.\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{7}{\int }_{0}^{1}3y+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{7}{[\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{7}(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{7}\cdot \frac{11}{6} \\  & =\frac{11}{21}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[3X+7Y] & =3\,\text{E}[X]+7\,\text{E}[Y] \\  & =3(0)+7(\frac{11}{21}) \\  & =0+\frac{11}{3} \\  & =\frac{11}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
